errors.description: The collar leaves and the gorge seam sit above the top frame edge, so the buttonhole's height relative to the gorge cannot be measured in-frame — only its height relative to the lapel edge. The blueprint does place its two marks well below the collar, and the render is consistent with that, but the absolute reference point is outside the crop.
errors.expected: buttonhole position measurable against the gorge, per the drawing
errors.actual: gorge cropped above frame; position measurable only against the lapel edge
errors.correction: acceptable; the mandated tight crop necessarily excludes the gorge, and left/right position parity — which is what this option specifies — is fully verifiable

errors.description: The buttonholes themselves are small in absolute area (roughly 1% each); what dominates is the pair of lapel faces that carry them. For a position-type option specified across BOTH lapels this is the correct trade-off — the frame must be wide enough to show both sides at once — but a viewer must look at two small marks rather than one large feature.
errors.expected: the craft option dominating 40-80% of frame
errors.actual: the two lapel faces carrying the buttonholes fill roughly 65% of frame; the buttonhole marks themselves are small
errors.correction: no action; this is the tightest framing that still proves the 'both sides' specification

ATTEMPT 2 — ADVERSARIAL RE-READ vs /images/blueprints/supplier/68b420f69832__0543__Right_Left_bttn_hole.jpg.

THE ATTEMPT-1 CRITICAL FAILURE IS FULLY RESOLVED. Attempt 1 traced the blueprint's red position markers into the cloth and produced two saturated red buttonholes resembling applied plastic tags. Attempt 2 renders both buttonholes as genuine worked buttonholes stitched in navy thread matching the hopsack — tonal, reading unmistakably as stitched cloth. There is now NO red anywhere in the frame. This confirms that the fix for annotation-colour tracing is to state explicitly that the drawing's red means position, not colour.

THE ATTEMPT-1 MAJOR FAILURES ARE ALSO RESOLVED: the necktie, chin and neck are gone, and the crop is now a tight horizontal band across both lapel faces at buttonhole height, with only a narrow strip of plain white shirt between them. Nothing competes with the option.

EVERY LOCKED FEATURE RE-VERIFIED AFTER THE CORRECTION (checking the fix broke nothing):
- Count: still exactly one buttonhole per lapel. It did not drift to two-on-one-side or to none, which was the main risk when re-rolling a count-sensitive option.
- Symmetry: the two buttonholes sit at matching height and matching distance from their respective lapel edges.
- Lapel family: still a notch lapel; no drift to peak or shawl.
- Face: still the front.
- Annotation: no numbers, arrows, leader lines, ticks or text.

ATTEMPTED REJECTIONS THAT FAILED: (1) Are these real worked buttonholes or just dark dashes painted on? At full resolution each shows a bar-tacked end and a stitched gimp edge raised above the weave — genuine construction. (2) Did the tighter crop lose the 'both sides' proof? No — both lapels and both buttonholes are simultaneously in frame, which is the entire point of this option. (3) Is the cloth still sport-coat appropriate? Yes, open hopsack basketweave.

No critical or major findings remain.
